answer: The shared yield pool is a meadow: each identity grazes only a small daily quota, and the meadow regrows at a fixed rate, so a Sybil farm combined grazing hits the carrying capacity and throttles all clones at once. Every draw also locks a share in a vault that opens only after several epochs of verified honest work, so clones pay waiting cost to cash out. Planting a yarrow marker, a small one-time verifiable commitment bound to the identity, proves the grazer is a distinct participant, not a throwaway copy. Attackers can spawn thousands of mouths, but the meadow cannot feed them all.
